title: 9 Hunters

sources.label: HOW TO PLAY 9 Hunters Build In Auto Chess | 3 Variations

body:
# 9 Hunters

Hunters are the classic glass-cannon board: a wall of ranged physical damage that
has to kill the enemy before the enemy closes in. You three-star five or six
cheap hunters early, coast through the mid game on that spike, and then hunt down
the ninth hunter to unlock the full trait. At 9 Hunters every shot is precise,
enemy armour drops, and hits knock targets back while adding an extra attack — a
board that pushes the enemy away while shredding them. The build is one of the
strongest things in the game before round 35; the whole challenge is surviving
the ultra-late game, where assassins and warriors punish how squishy you are.

## When to commit

Two signals tell you hunters are the right call. First, you open the game with a
lot of hunters showing up in your shop — a natural sign the pool is flowing your
way. Second, and more important, you find the **Telescope** (a tier-2 neutral).
Telescope gives the Dwarf bonus to Sniper and one other hunter, granting massive
bonus range and distance-scaling damage. Without Telescope the ceiling on the
whole build drops hard, so treat it as the make-or-break item.

## Core Units

Six cheap hunters form the early three-star core; Tidehunter is the payoff ninth.

| Unit | Cost | Role |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Sniper | 2 | Dwarf carry — highest single-target damage |
| Windranger | 2 | Telescope holder, multi-target stuns |
| Beastmaster | 2 | Front-line anchor, summons |
| Bounty Hunter | 1 | Economy engine (bonus gold on first kill) |
| Hoodwink | 1 | Cheap hunter body |
| Mirana | 1 | Middle position, AoE |
| Medusa | 4 | Late-game carry + Naga magic resist |
| Broodmother | 4 | Optional purple hunter |
| Tidehunter | 5 | The ninth hunter — Ravage + knockback |

Two-star Beastmaster is your stability breakpoint — before it lands your front
line folds. Bounty Hunter is a hidden economy engine: every *new copy* of Bounty
Hunter earns bonus gold on its first kill, so cycling one-, two-, and three-star
Bounty Hunters can net roughly 10 extra gold over the game.

## Items

- **Telescope** — the priority item, given to Windranger (not Sniper, who is
  already a Dwarf) so a second hunter gains the range/damage bonus.
- **Desolator** on Sniper for armour reduction and raw damage.
- **Havoc Hammer** (tier 5) — pure damage to punch through armour-stacking
  warriors; put it on Sniper, Windranger, or Medusa.
- **Necronomicon** on Beastmaster (great with Refresher) for extra tanky summons.
- **Vanguard** early on a front-liner like Tidehunter for survivability.
- Anti-priest tech: a **Gossamer/mind-control cloak** on your best carry so the
  enemy can't steal your Beastmaster or Medusa.

## Relics

- **Dungeon Key** is the standout — it lets you re-dismiss and re-roll synergy dismissals
  repeatedly, so at level 9 you can re-dismiss the legendary Warriors to spike your
  odds of hitting Tidehunter.
- Skip Magical Sprout — hunters want to roll after round 15, not hoard seeds.
- Doomling is a greedy option only if you are above 80% HP; keep your HP higher
  than your current gold percentage or the second Doomling conversion can
  actively hurt you.

## Leveling / Roll Plan

Decide on round 4-5 whether you are a win-streak or lose-streak hunter — the
guide favours lose-streak for steadier income. Either way, **never go past level
5 in the early game**; tier-1 odds fall off at 5 and 6, and tier-2 odds peak at
5. Sit at level 5 after round 10 and roll toward three stars. On round 15, dismiss
the Warriors (four units out of the pool, the best dismissal for tier-1 odds) and take
the roll-cost-reduction talent, which can save 8+ gold per three-star. Don't
force the last three-star unless it's Beastmaster or Sniper. Push to level 9 to
find Tidehunter; if he never appears, the fallback ninth hunter is two Wizards at
level 10 (far more expensive) or a three-elf splash with Dark Willow.

## Positioning / Matchup Notes

Spread the board wide in a shallow corner so the two Dwarf-ranged units fire from
maximum distance and a single Tiny toss or Tidehunter Ravage can't catch the
whole team. Sniper and Windranger sit in the back corners; Beastmaster and
Hoodwink hold the front; Mirana sits central for coverage. Against **assassins**
in the late game, do the opposite — ball up tight so they can't leap past your
front line to your carries. Hunters hard-counter **elves** (low evasion uptime
against precise shots) but lose to **warriors** (out-tank and reflect) and to
burst **assassins**. Since the board can't beat everyone, position and itemise to
farm the matchups you *can* win and let the lobby thin out the rest.
